title: When geometry becomes an engine
mathematical_role: Orient the reader to metric evolution under Ricci flow and the distinction between smoothing and curvature concentration.
learning_objective: Recognize that Ricci flow is a time-dependent evolution of the metric and that singular behavior is associated with concentrated curvature rather than a decorative marker on a static shape.
literal_semantics: The plate is intended only to indicate that geometry changes and that curvature concentration is a distinct event requiring analysis.
nonliteral_semantics: The drawn surface is not a literal three-manifold or metric realization.
The grid spacing is not a curvature scale.
The highlighted point is not a computed singularity.
The lower waveform is not a Ricci-flow solution or curvature trace.

notes: Current predecessor contract only; successor rendering remains to be implemented under ADR-0018.

reproducibility_notes: The committed SVG bytes are preserved, but no domain renderer or mathematical evolution source is bound to the predecessor image.

accessibility.alt_text: A curved geometry smoothing under Ricci flow while concentrated curvature signals a possible singularity.
accessibility.long_description: The current predecessor is a schematic static plate. It gestures toward metric smoothing and curvature concentration but does not show a time-indexed metric, curvature field, scale, or computed singularity. The replacement must make the temporal and curvature semantics explicit.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: Pedagogical orientation to the roles of smoothing and curvature concentration in the Ricci-flow narrative.
not_claimed: A proof of any Hamilton-Perelman theorem

supersession_reason: The current static schematic does not encode the time-dependent geometric semantics asserted by its teaching role.
